mapping_notes: An 'error' here is a data-quality issue that causes customer-facing downtime. 72 issues per year, 15% of them customer-facing, so error_rate_before = 15% of 72 records-or-events.
Cost of one such issue = 2 hours x ($6 billion / 8,760 hours x 5% affected) = $68,493.15 (we do not round it; Forrester rounds the hourly figure).

Forrester applies the resolution-speed gain (80% / 85% / 90%) to the downtime hours. In our formula that is the same as lowering the share of costly issues, so error_rate_after = 15% x (1 - 90%) = 1.5% at the Year 3 level, and adoption_by_year = 80/90, 85/90, 100 reproduces the ramp. This is a reinterpretation of resolution speed as avoided issues; the product of terms is identical.
